intro: Map apps tell a wheelchair user how far a route is. They don't say whether it has broken slabs, cobblestones, a curb with no ramp, or a flight of steps. RollMap does.
monaco: Here is a trip in Monaco. Hilly, full of steps, and old paving. The coloured lines are a comfort layer, built from rides.
short: The shortest walk uses five flights of steps, and over four hundred metres of rough ground. Impossible in a wheelchair.
smooth: RollMap finds a step-free route that is far smoother. Comfort eighty-nine, versus fifty-three.
profiles: Each profile weighs roughness differently. Manual chair, power chair, or stroller.
sensing: Now the sensing. A phone in the wheelchair bag is all it takes. For this video, we play a simulated sensor stream, through the exact pipeline the phone runs.
iso: The live comfort score uses I S O twenty-six thirty-one weighting. The international standard for how a seated body feels vibration.
surface: A small neural network on the phone names the surface. Smooth, cracked, pavers, or gravel.
orientation: It works with the phone in any orientation. Gravity tells it which way is down.
jolts: Curb drops and potholes are caught as jolts. A single sharp shock that stands out from rough ground.
summary: After the ride, you get the vibration dose, and the health zone. For people who roll all day, that is a health issue, not just comfort.
reports: Every problem becomes a ready-to-send repair report for the city, with the location and the measured shock. Copy it, share it, or export it for three-one-one systems.
real: We checked it on real, public phone rides. On four bike rides in India, it ranked the road that photos show is failing as the worst, in every single ride, and flagged all fifteen photographed defects. On car drives with labelled potholes, its vibration peaks told real potholes apart from other bumps.
honest: Everything is open and explainable, and every simulated part is clearly labelled.
outro: RollMap. Measure what a rider actually feels, route around it, and get it fixed. It runs in any phone browser, with no install.
